As the `[apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply)` tactic is a command for constructing function
applications interactively, the `[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro)` tactic is a command for
constructing function abstractions interactively (i.e., terms of the
form `fun x => e`). As with lambda abstraction notation, the
`[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro)` tactic allows us to use an implicit `match`.

```lean
example (p q : α → Prop) : (∃ x, p x ∧ q x) → ∃ x, q x ∧ p x := byα:Sort u_1p:α → Propq:α → Prop⊢ [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro)[∃](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) x[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) p x [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q x[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) → [∃](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) x[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) q x [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) p x
[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro) ⟨w, hpw, hqw⟩α:Sort u_1p:α → Propq:α → Propw:αhpw:p whqw:q w⊢ [∃](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) x[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) q x [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) p x
[exact](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#exact) ⟨w, hqw, hpw⟩All goals completed! 🐙
```

The `[intros](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intros)` tactic can be used without any arguments, in which
case, it chooses names and introduces as many variables as it can. You
will see an example of this in a moment.

The `[assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)` tactic looks through the assumptions in context of
the current goal, and if there is one matching the conclusion, it
applies it.

```lean
[variable](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Namespaces-and-Sections/#Lean___Parser___Command___variable) (x y z w : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero))
```


It will unify metavariables in the conclusion if necessary:

```lean
[variable](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Namespaces-and-Sections/#Lean___Parser___Command___variable) (x y z w : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero))
```

Note that names automatically generated by Lean are inaccessible by default. The motivation is to
ensure your tactic proofs do not rely on automatically generated names, and are consequently more robust.
However, you can use the combinator `[unhygienic](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#unhygienic)` to disable this restriction.

You can also use the `[rename_i](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#rename_i)` tactic to rename the most recent inaccessible names in your context.
In the following example, the tactic `[rename_i](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#rename_i) h1 _ h2` renames two of the last three hypotheses in
your context.

The `[rfl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rfl)` tactic solves goals that are reflexive relations applied to definitionally equal arguments.
Equality is reflexive:

```lean
example (y : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : (fun x : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) => 0) y = 0 := byy:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ (fun x => 0) y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0
[rfl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rfl)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

Another tactic that is sometimes useful is the `[revert](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#revert)` tactic,
which is, in a sense, an inverse to `[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro)`:

```lean
example (x : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : x = x := byx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x
[revert](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#revert) x⊢ ∀ (x : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)), x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x
[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro) yy:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y
[rfl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rfl)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

After `[revert](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#revert) x`, the proof state is:

⊢ ∀ (x : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)), x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x

After `[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro) y`, it is:

y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y

Moving a hypothesis into the goal yields an implication:

```lean
example (x y : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) (h : x = y) : y = x := byx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h:x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y⊢ y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x
[revert](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#revert) hx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y → y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x
[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro) h₁x:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y⊢ y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x
-- goal is x y : Nat, h₁ : x = y ⊢ y = x
[apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Eq.symm](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___symm)x:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y⊢ x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y
[assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

After `[revert](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#revert) h`, the proof state is:

x:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y → y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x

After `[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro) h₁`, it is:

x:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y⊢ y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x

But `[revert](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#revert)` is even more clever, in that it will revert not only an
element of the context but also all the subsequent elements of the
context that depend on it. For example, reverting `x` in the example
above brings `h` along with it:

```lean
example (x y : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) (h : x = y) : y = x := byx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h:x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y⊢ y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x
[revert](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#revert) xy:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ ∀ (x : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)), x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y → y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x
[intros](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intros)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)x✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h✝:x✝ [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y⊢ y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x✝
[apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Eq.symm](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___symm)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)x✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h✝:x✝ [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y⊢ x✝ [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y
[assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

After `[revert](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#revert) x`, the goal is:

y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ ∀ (x : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)), x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y → y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x

You can also revert multiple elements of the context at once:

```lean
example (x y : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) (h : x = y) : y = x := byx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h:x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y⊢ y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x
[revert](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#revert) x y⊢ ∀ (x y : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)), x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y → y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x
[intros](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intros)x✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h✝:x✝ [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y✝⊢ y✝ [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x✝
[apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Eq.symm](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___symm)x✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h✝:x✝ [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y✝⊢ x✝ [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y✝
[assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

After `[revert](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#revert) x y`, the goal is:

⊢ ∀ (x y : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)), x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y → y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x

You can only `[revert](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#revert)` an element of the local context, that is, a
local variable or hypothesis. But you can replace an arbitrary
expression in the goal by a fresh variable using the `[generalize](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#generalize)`
tactic:

```lean
example : 3 = 3 := by⊢ 3 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 3
[generalize](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#generalize) 3 = xx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x
[revert](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#revert) x⊢ ∀ (x : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)), x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x
[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro) yy:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ y [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) y
[rfl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rfl)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

In particular, after `[generalize](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#generalize)`, the goal is

x:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x

The mnemonic in the notation above is that you are generalizing the
goal by setting `3` to an arbitrary variable `x`. Be careful: not
every generalization preserves the validity of the goal. Here,
`[generalize](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#generalize)` replaces a goal that could be proved using
`rfl` with one that is not provable:

```lean
example : 2 + 3 = 5 := by⊢ 2 [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) 3 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 5
[generalize](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#generalize) 3 = xx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ 2 [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 5
[sorry](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#sorry)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

In this example, the `[sorry](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#sorry)` tactic is the analogue of the `sorry`
proof term. It closes the current goal, producing the usual warning
that `sorry` has been used. To preserve the validity of the previous
goal, the `[generalize](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#generalize)` tactic allows us to record the fact that
`3` has been replaced by `x`. All you need to do is to provide a
label, and `[generalize](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#generalize)` uses it to store the assignment in the local
context:

```lean
example : 2 + 3 = 5 := by⊢ 2 [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) 3 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 5
[generalize](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#generalize) h : 3 = xx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h:3 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x⊢ 2 [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 5
[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw) [← hx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h:3 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x⊢ 2 [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) 3 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 5]All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

Following `[generalize](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#generalize) h : 3 = x`, `h` is a proof that `3 = x`:

x:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h:3 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x⊢ 2 [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 5

Here the rewriting tactic `[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw)` uses `h` to replace
`x` by `3` again. The `[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw)` tactic will be discussed below.

### 5.3. More Tactics {#tpil-more-tactics}

Some additional tactics are useful for constructing and destructing
propositions and data. For example, when applied to a goal of the form
`p ∨ q`, you use tactics such as `[apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)` and
`[apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inr](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)`. Conversely, the `[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases)` tactic can be used to decompose a
disjunction:

```lean
example (p q : Prop) : p ∨ q → q ∨ p := byp:Propq:Prop⊢ p [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) q → q [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) p
[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro) hp:Propq:Proph:p [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) q⊢ q [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) p
```

```lean

```

Note that the syntax is similar to the one used in `match` expressions.
The new subgoals can be solved in any order:


You can also use a (unstructured) `[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases)` without the `with` and a tactic
for each alternative:


The (unstructured) `[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases)` is particularly useful when you can close several
subgoals using the same tactic:

```lean
example (p : Prop) : p ∨ p → p := byp:Prop⊢ p [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) p → p
[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro) hp:Proph:p [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) p⊢ p
[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases) hinlp:Proph✝:p⊢ pinrp:Proph✝:p⊢ p
[repeat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#repeat) [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

You can also use the combinator `tac1 ``<;>`` tac2` to apply `tac2` to each
subgoal produced by tactic `tac1`:

```lean
example (p : Prop) : p ∨ p → p := byp:Prop⊢ p [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) p → p
[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro) hp:Proph:p [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) p⊢ p
[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases) hinlp:Proph✝:p⊢ pinrp:Proph✝:p⊢ p <;>inlp:Proph✝:p⊢ pinrp:Proph✝:p⊢ p [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

The `[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases)` tactic can also be used to
decompose a conjunction:

```lean
example (p q : Prop) : p ∧ q → q ∧ p := byp:Propq:Prop⊢ p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q → q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) p
[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro) hp:Propq:Proph:p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q⊢ q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) p
[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases) h with
| [intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) hp hq =>introp:Propq:Prophp:phq:q⊢ q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) p [constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)intro.leftp:Propq:Prophp:phq:q⊢ qintro.rightp:Propq:Prophp:phq:q⊢ p; [exact](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#exact) hqintro.rightp:Propq:Prophp:phq:q⊢ p; [exact](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#exact) hpAll goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

In this example, there is only one goal after the `[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases)` tactic is
applied, with `h`` : ``p ∧ q` replaced by a pair of assumptions,
`hp`` : ``p` and `hq`` : ``q`:

introp:Propq:Prophp:phq:q⊢ q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) p

The `[constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)` tactic applies the unique
constructor for conjunction, `[And.intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro)`.

With these tactics, an
example from the previous section can be rewritten as follows:


You will see in [Inductive Types](https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/Inductive-Types/#inductive-types) that
these tactics are quite general. The `[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases)` tactic can be used to
decompose any element of an inductively defined type; `[constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)`
always applies the first applicable constructor of an inductively defined type.
For example, you can use `[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases)` and `[constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)` with an existential quantifier:

```lean
example (p q : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → Prop) : (∃ x, p x) → ∃ x, p x ∨ q x := byp:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → Propq:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → Prop⊢ [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro)[∃](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) x[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) p x[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) → [∃](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) x[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) p x [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) q x
```

Here, the `[constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)` tactic leaves the first component of the
existential assertion, the value of `x`, implicit. It is represented
by a metavariable, which should be instantiated later on. In the
previous example, the proper value of the metavariable is determined
by the tactic `[exact](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#exact) px`, since `px` has type `p x`. If you want
to specify a witness to the existential quantifier explicitly, you can
use the `exists` tactic instead:


These tactics can be used on data just as well as propositions. In the
next example, they are used to define functions which swap the
components of the product and sum types:

```lean

[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases) pmkα:Type ?u.6β:Type ?u.5fst✝:αsnd✝:β⊢ β [×](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Tuples/#Prod___mk) α
```

Note that up to the names we have chosen for the variables, the
definitions are identical to the proofs of the analogous propositions
for conjunction and disjunction. The `[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases)` tactic will also do a
case distinction on a natural number:

```lean
[open](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Namespaces-and-Sections/#Lean___Parser___Command___open) Nat
```

The `[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases)` tactic, and its companion, the `induction` tactic, are discussed in greater detail in
the [Tactics for Inductive Types](https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/Inductive-Types/#tactics-for-inductive-types) section.

The `[contradiction](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#contradiction)` tactic searches for a contradiction among the hypotheses of the current goal:

```lean
example (p q : Prop) : p ∧ ¬ p → q := byp:Propq:Prop⊢ p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) [¬](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Not)p → q
[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro) hp:Propq:Proph:p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) [¬](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Not)p⊢ q
[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases) hintrop:Propq:Propleft✝:pright✝:[¬](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Not)p⊢ q
[contradiction](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#contradiction)All goals completed! 🐙
```

### 5.4. Structuring Tactic Proofs {#tpil-structuring-tactic-proofs}

Tactics often provide an efficient way of building a proof, but long
sequences of instructions can obscure the structure of the
argument. In this section, we describe some means that help provide
structure to a tactic-style proof, making such proofs more readable
and robust.

One thing that is nice about Lean's proof-writing syntax is that it is
possible to mix term-style and tactic-style proofs, and pass between
the two freely. For example, the tactics `[apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply)` and `[exact](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#exact)`
expect arbitrary terms, which you can write using `have`, `show`,
and so on. Conversely, when writing an arbitrary Lean term, you can
always invoke the tactic mode by inserting a `by`
block. The following is a somewhat toy example:

```lean
example (p q r : Prop) : p ∧ (q ∨ r) → (p ∧ q) ∨ (p ∧ r) := byp:Propq:Propr:Prop⊢ p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)q [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) r[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) → p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r
[intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intro) hp:Propq:Propr:Proph:p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)q [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) r[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)⊢ p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r
[exact](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#exact)
have hp : p := h.[left](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro)
have hqr : q ∨ r := h.[right](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro)
```

In fact, there is a `show` tactic, which is similar to the
`show` expression in a proof term. It simply declares the type of the
goal that is about to be solved, while remaining in tactic
mode.

The `show` tactic can actually be used to rewrite a goal to something definitionally equivalent:

```lean
example (n : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : n + 1 = [Nat.succ](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) n := byn:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ n [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) 1 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) n.[succ](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)
[show](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#show) [Nat.succ](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) n = [Nat.succ](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) nn:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ n.[succ](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) n.[succ](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)
[rfl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rfl)All goals completed! 🐙
```

There is also a `have` tactic, which introduces a new subgoal, just as when writing proof terms:

The types in a `have` tactic can be omitted, so you can write
`have hp := h.left` and `have hqr := h.right`. In fact, with this
notation, you can even omit both the type and the label, in which case
the new fact is introduced with the label `this`:


Lean also has a `let` tactic, which is similar to the `have`
tactic, but is used to introduce local definitions instead of
auxiliary facts. It is the tactic analogue of a `let` in a proof
term:

```lean
example : ∃ x, x + 2 = 8 := by⊢ [∃](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) x[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) x [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) 2 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 8
[let](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#let) a : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) := 3 * 2a:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) := 3 [*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk) 2⊢ [∃](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) x[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Quantifiers/#Exists___intro) x [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) 2 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 8
[exists](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#exists) aAll goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

As with `have`, you can leave the type implicit by writing
`let a := 3 * 2`. The difference between `let` and `have` is that
`let` introduces a local definition in the context, so that the
definition of the local declaration can be unfolded in the proof.

We have used `.` to create nested tactic blocks. In a nested block,
Lean focuses on the first goal, and generates an error if it has not
been fully solved at the end of the block. This can be helpful in
indicating the separate proofs of multiple subgoals introduced by a
tactic. The notation `.` is whitespace sensitive and relies on the indentation
to detect whether the tactic block ends. Alternatively, you can
define tactic blocks using curly braces and semicolons:


```lean

```

It is useful to use indentation to structure proof: every time a tactic
leaves more than one subgoal, we separate the remaining subgoals by
enclosing them in blocks and indenting. Thus if the application of
theorem `foo` to a single goal produces four subgoals, one would
expect the proof to look like this:

```
  apply foo
  . <proof of first goal>
  . <proof of second goal>
  . <proof of third goal>
  . <proof of final goal>
```

or

```
  apply foo
  case <tag of first goal>  => <proof of first goal>
  case <tag of second goal> => <proof of second goal>
  case <tag of third goal>  => <proof of third goal>
  case <tag of final goal>  => <proof of final goal>
```

or

```
  apply foo
  { <proof of first goal>  }
  { <proof of second goal> }
  { <proof of third goal>  }
  { <proof of final goal>  }
```

### 5.5. Tactic Combinators {#tpil-tactic-combinators}

*Tactic combinators* are operations that form new tactics from old
ones. A sequencing combinator is already implicit in the `by` block:

```lean
example (p q : Prop) (hp : p) : p ∨ q :=
byp:Propq:Prophp:p⊢ p [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) q [apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)p:Propq:Prophp:p⊢ p; [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

Here, `[apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl); [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)` is functionally equivalent to a
single tactic which first applies `[apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)` and then applies
`[assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)`.

In `t₁ ``<;>`` t₂`, the `<;>` operator provides a *parallel* version of the sequencing operation:
`t₁` is applied to the current goal, and then `t₂` is applied to *all* the resulting subgoals:

```lean
example (p q : Prop) (hp : p) (hq : q) : p ∧ q :=
byp:Propq:Prophp:phq:q⊢ p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q [constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)leftp:Propq:Prophp:phq:q⊢ prightp:Propq:Prophp:phq:q⊢ q <;>leftp:Propq:Prophp:phq:q⊢ prightp:Propq:Prophp:phq:q⊢ q [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

This is especially useful when the resulting goals can be finished off
in a uniform way, or, at least, when it is possible to make progress
on all of them uniformly.

The `first`` | t₁ | t₂ | ... | tₙ` applies each `tᵢ` until one succeeds, or else fails:

```lean
example (p q : Prop) (hp : p) : p ∨ q := byp:Propq:Prophp:p⊢ p [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) q
[first](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#first) | [apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)p:Propq:Prophp:p⊢ p; [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙 | [apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) Or.inr; [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)
```

```lean
example (p q : Prop) (hq : q) : p ∨ q := byp:Propq:Prophq:q⊢ p [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) q
[first](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#first) | [apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)p:Propq:Prophq:q⊢ p; [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)p:Propq:Prophq:q⊢ p | [apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inr](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)p:Propq:Prophq:q⊢ q; [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

In the first example, the left branch succeeds, whereas in the second one, it is the right one that succeeds.
In the next three examples, the same compound tactic succeeds in each case:

```lean
example (p q r : Prop) (hp : p) : p ∨ q ∨ r := byp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:p⊢ p [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) q [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) r
[repeat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#repeat) ([first](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#first) | [apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)p:Propq:Propr:Prophp:p⊢ p; [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙 | [apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) Or.inr | [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption))
```

```lean
example (p q r : Prop) (hq : q) : p ∨ q ∨ r := byp:Propq:Propr:Prophq:q⊢ p [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) q [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) r
[repeat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#repeat) ([first](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#first) | [apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)p:Propq:Propr:Prophq:q⊢ q; [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙 | [apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inr](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)p:Propq:Propr:Prophq:q⊢ q [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) r | [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption))
```

```lean
example (p q r : Prop) (hr : r) : p ∨ q ∨ r := byp:Propq:Propr:Prophr:r⊢ p [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) q [∨](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) r
[repeat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#repeat) ([first](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#first) | [apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)p:Propq:Propr:Prophr:r⊢ r; [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)p:Propq:Propr:Prophr:r⊢ q | [apply](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#apply) [Or.inr](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl)p:Propq:Propr:Prophr:r⊢ r | [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙)
```

```lean

```

The tactic tries to solve the left disjunct immediately by assumption;
if that fails, it tries to focus on the right disjunct; and if that
doesn't work, it invokes the assumption tactic.

You will have no doubt noticed by now that tactics can fail. Indeed,
it is the “failure” state that causes the *first* combinator to
backtrack and try the next tactic. The `[try](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#try)` combinator builds a
tactic that always succeeds, though possibly in a trivial way:
`try`` t` executes `t` and reports success, even if `t` fails. It is
equivalent to `first``| t |``skip`, where `skip` is a tactic that does
nothing (and succeeds in doing so). In the next example, the second
`[constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)` succeeds on the right conjunct `q ∧ r` (remember that
disjunction and conjunction associate to the right) but fails on the
first. The `[try](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#try)` tactic ensures that the sequential composition
succeeds:

```lean
example (p q r : Prop) (hp : p) (hq : q) (hr : r) : p ∧ q ∧ r := byp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r
[constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)leftp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ prightp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r <;>leftp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ prightp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r ([try](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#try) [constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)right.leftp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ qright.rightp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ r) <;>leftp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ pright.leftp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ qright.rightp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ r [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

Be careful: `repeat`` (``try`` t)` will loop forever, because the inner tactic never fails.

In a proof, there are often multiple goals outstanding. Parallel
sequencing is one way to arrange it so that a single tactic is applied
to multiple goals, but there are other ways to do this. For example,
`all_goals`` t` applies `t` to all open goals:

```lean
example (p q r : Prop) (hp : p) (hq : q) (hr : r) : p ∧ q ∧ r := byp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r
[constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)leftp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ prightp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r
[all_goals](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#all_goals) ([try](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#try) [constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)right.leftp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ qright.rightp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ r)
[all_goals](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#all_goals) [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

In this case, the `any_goals` tactic provides a more robust solution.
It is similar to `all_goals`, except it succeeds if its argument
succeeds on at least one goal:

```lean
example (p q r : Prop) (hp : p) (hq : q) (hr : r) : p ∧ q ∧ r := byp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r
[constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)leftp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ prightp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r
[any_goals](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#any_goals) [constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)right.leftp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ qright.rightp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ r
[any_goals](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#any_goals) [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

The first tactic in the `by` block below repeatedly splits
conjunctions:

```lean
example (p q r : Prop) (hp : p) (hq : q) (hr : r) :
p ∧ ((p ∧ q) ∧ r) ∧ (q ∧ r ∧ p) := byp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro)[(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro)p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) p
[repeat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#repeat) ([any_goals](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#any_goals) [constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)right.right.right.rightp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ p)
[all_goals](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#all_goals) [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

In fact, we can compress the full tactic down to one line:

```lean
example (p q r : Prop) (hp : p) (hq : q) (hr : r) :
p ∧ ((p ∧ q) ∧ r) ∧ (q ∧ r ∧ p) := byp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro)[(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro)p [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) q [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) r [∧](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#And___intro) p
[repeat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#repeat) ([any_goals](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#any_goals) ([first](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/The-Tactic-Language/#first) | [constructor](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#constructor)right.right.right.rightp:Propq:Propr:Prophp:phq:qhr:r⊢ p | [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙))
```

```lean

```

The combinator `focus`` t` ensures that `t` only effects the current
goal, temporarily hiding the others from the scope. So, if `t`
ordinarily only effects the current goal, `focus`` (``all_goals`` t)` has
the same effect as `t`.

### 5.6. Rewriting {#tpil-rewriting}

The `rw` tactic and the `simp` tactic
were introduced briefly in [Calculational Proofs]](#tpil-calculational-proofs). In this
section and the next, we discuss them in greater detail.

The `rw` tactic provides a basic mechanism for applying
substitutions to goals and hypotheses, providing a convenient and
efficient way of working with equality. The most basic form of the
tactic is `rw`` [t]`, where `t` is a term whose type asserts an
equality. For example, `t` can be a hypothesis `h : x = y` in the
context; it can be a general lemma, like
`[add_comm](https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/Inductive-Types/#add_comm) : ∀ x y, x + y = y + x`, in which the rewrite tactic tries to find suitable
instantiations of `x` and `y`; or it can be any compound term
asserting a concrete or general equation. In the following example, we
use this basic form to rewrite the goal using a hypothesis.

```lean
[variable](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Namespaces-and-Sections/#Lean___Parser___Command___variable) (k : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) (f : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero))
```

```lean
example (h₁ : f 0 = 0) (h₂ : k = 0) : f k = 0 := byk:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)f:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:f 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0h₂:k [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ f k [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0
[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw) [h₂k:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)f:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:f 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0h₂:k [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ f 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0]k:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)f:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:f 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0h₂:k [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ f 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0 -- replace k with 0
[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw) [h₁k:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)f:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:f 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0h₂:k [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0]All goals completed! 🐙 -- replace f 0 with 0
```

```lean

```

In the example above, the first use of `[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw)` replaces `k` with
`0` in the goal `f k = 0`. Then, the second one replaces `f 0`
with `0`. The tactic automatically closes any goal of the form
`t = t`. Here is an example of rewriting using a compound expression:

```lean
example (x y : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) (p : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → Prop) (q : Prop) (h : q → x = y)
(h' : p y) (hq : q) : p x := byx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)p:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → Propq:Proph:q → x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) yh':p yhq:q⊢ p x
[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw) [h hqx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)p:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → Propq:Proph:q → x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) yh':p yhq:q⊢ p y]x:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)p:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → Propq:Proph:q → x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) yh':p yhq:q⊢ p y; [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

Here, `h hq` establishes the equation `x = y`.

Multiple rewrites can be combined using the notation `rw`` [t_1, ..., t_n]`,
which is just shorthand for `rw``[t_1]; ...;``rw`` [t_n]`. The previous example can be written as follows:

```lean
[variable](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Namespaces-and-Sections/#Lean___Parser___Command___variable) (k : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) (f : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero))
```

```lean
example (h₁ : f 0 = 0) (h₂ : k = 0) : f k = 0 := byk:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)f:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:f 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0h₂:k [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ f k [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0
[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw) [h₂,k:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)f:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:f 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0h₂:k [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ f 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0 h₁k:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)f:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:f 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0h₂:k [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0]All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

By default, `[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw)` uses an equation in the forward direction, matching
the left-hand side with an expression, and replacing it with the
right-hand side. The notation `←t` can be used to instruct the
tactic to use the equality `t` in the reverse direction.

```lean
[variable](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Namespaces-and-Sections/#Lean___Parser___Command___variable) (a b : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) (f : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero))
```

```lean
example (h₁ : a = b) (h₂ : f a = 0) : f b = 0 := bya:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)b:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)f:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) bh₂:f a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ f b [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0
[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw) [←h₁,a:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)b:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)f:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) bh₂:f a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ f a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0 h₂a:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)b:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)f:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h₁:a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) bh₂:f a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0]All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean

```

In this example, the term `←h₁` instructs the rewriter to replace
`b` with `a`. In the editors, you can type the backwards arrow as
`\l`. You can also use the ASCII equivalent, `<-`.

Sometimes the left-hand side of an identity can match more than one
subterm in the pattern, in which case the `rw` tactic chooses the
first match it finds when traversing the term. If that is not the one
you want, you can use additional arguments to specify the appropriate
subterm.

```lean
example (a b c : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : a + b + c = a + c + b := bya:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)b:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)c:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ a [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) b [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) c [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) a [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) c [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) b
```

```lean

```

In the first example above, the first step rewrites `a + b + c` to
`a`` + (``b + c``)`. The next step applies commutativity to the term
`b + c`; without specifying the argument, the tactic would instead rewrite
`a`` + (``b + c``)` to `(``b + c``) + ``a`. Finally, the last step applies
associativity in the reverse direction, rewriting `a`` + (``c`` + ``b``)` to
`a + c + b`. The next two examples instead apply associativity to
move the parenthesis to the right on both sides, and then switch `b`
and `c`. Notice that the last example specifies that the rewrite
should take place on the right-hand side by specifying the second
argument to `Nat.add_comm`.

By default, the `[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw)` tactic affects only the goal. The notation
`rw`` [t] ``at`` h` applies the rewrite

```lean

[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw) [Nat.add_zerof:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)a:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h:a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ f a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) f 0] at hf:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)a:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h:a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ f a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) f 0
[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw) [hf:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)a:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h:a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0⊢ f 0 [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) f 0]All goals completed! 🐙
```


The first step, `[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw) [Nat.add_zero] at h`, rewrites the hypothesis `a + 0 = 0` to `a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0`.
Then the new hypothesis `a [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0` is used to rewrite the goal to `f 0`` = ``f 0`.

The `[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw)` tactic is not restricted to propositions.
In the following example, we use `rw`` [h] ``at`` t` to rewrite the hypothesis `t : Tuple α n` to `t : Tuple α`` 0`.

```lean
def Tuple (α : Type) (n : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) :=
{ as : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α // as.[length](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___length) = n }
```

```lean
example (n : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) (h : n = 0) (t : Tuple α n) : Tuple α 0 := byα:Typen:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h:n [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0t:Tuple α n⊢ Tuple α 0
[rw](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#rw) [hα:Typen:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h:n [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0t:Tuple α 0⊢ Tuple α 0] at tα:Typen:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)h:n [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) 0t:Tuple α 0⊢ Tuple α 0
[exact](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#exact) tAll goals completed! 🐙
```

### 5.7. Using the Simplifier {#tpil-using-the-simplifier}

Whereas `rw` is designed as a surgical tool for manipulating a
goal, the simplifier offers a more powerful form of automation. A
number of identities in Lean's library have been tagged with the
`[simp]` attribute, and the `simp` tactic uses them to iteratively
rewrite subterms in an expression.

```lean
example (x y z : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : (x + 0) * (0 + y * 1 + z * 0) = x * y := byx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)z:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)⊢ [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk)x [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) 0[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) [*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk) [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk)0 [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) y [*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk) 1 [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) z [*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk) 0[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x [*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk) y
[simp](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#simp)All goals completed! 🐙
```

```lean
example (x y z : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) (p : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → Prop) (h : p (x * y))
: p ((x + 0) * (0 + y * 1 + z * 0)) := byx:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)z:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)p:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → Proph:p [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk)x [*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk) y[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk)⊢ p [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk)[(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk)x [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) 0[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) [*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk) [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk)0 [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) y [*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk) 1 [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) z [*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk) 0[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk)[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk)
[simp](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#simp)x:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)y:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)z:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)p:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → Proph:p [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk)x [*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk) y[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk)⊢ p [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk)x [*](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk) y[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HMul___mk); [assumption](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#assumption)All goals completed! 🐙
```
