Consequences of excluded middle include double-negation elimination,
proof by cases, and proof by contradiction, all of which are described
in the section on [classical logic]](#tpil-classical-logic).
The law of the excluded middle and propositional extensionality imply propositional completeness:

```lean
[open](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Namespaces-and-Sections/#Lean___Parser___Command___open) Classical
```

```lean
theorem propComplete (a : Prop) : a = [True](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Truth/#True___intro) ∨ a = [False](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Truth/#False) :=
[match](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Terms/Pattern-Matching/#Lean___Parser___Term___match) em a [with](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Terms/Pattern-Matching/#Lean___Parser___Term___match)
| [Or.inl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) ha =>
[Or.inl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) ([propext](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/The-Type-System/Propositions/#propext) ([Iff.intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Iff___intro) (fun _ => [True.intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Truth/#True___intro)) (fun _ => ha)))
| [Or.inr](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) hn =>
[Or.inr](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Or___inl) ([propext](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/The-Type-System/Propositions/#propext) ([Iff.intro](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Logical-Connectives/#Iff___intro) (fun h => hn h) (fun h => [False.elim](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Truth/#False___elim) h)))
```

Together with choice, we also get the stronger principle that every
proposition is decidable. Recall that the class of `[Decidable](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#Decidable___isFalse)`
propositions is defined as follows:

```lean
[namespace](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Namespaces-and-Sections/#Lean___Parser___Command___namespace) Hidden
```

```lean
class inductive Decidable (p : Prop) where
| isFalse (h : ¬p) : Decidable p
| isTrue (h : p) : Decidable p
```

```lean
end Hidden
```

In contrast to `p ∨ ¬ p`, which can only eliminate to `Prop`, the
type `[Decidable](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#Decidable___isFalse) p` is equivalent to the sum type `Sum p (¬ p)`, which
can eliminate to any type. It is this data that is needed to write an
if-then-else expression.

As an example of classical reasoning, we use `choose` to show that if
`f : α → β` is injective and `α` is inhabited, then `f` has a
left inverse. To define the left inverse `linv`, we use a dependent
if-then-else expression. Recall that `[if](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Terms/Conditionals/#termDepIfThenElse) h : c [then](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Terms/Conditionals/#termDepIfThenElse) t [else](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Terms/Conditionals/#termDepIfThenElse) e` is
notation for `dite c (fun h : c => t) (fun h : ¬ c => e)`. In the definition
of `linv`, choice is used twice: first, to show that
`(∃ a : α, f a = b)` is “decidable,” and then to choose an `a` such that
`f a = b`. Notice that `propDecidable` is a scoped instance and is activated
by the `[open](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Namespaces-and-Sections/#Lean___Parser___Command___open) Classical` command. We use this instance to justify
the `if`-`then`-`else` expression. (See also the discussion in
[Decidable Propositions]](#tpil-decidable-propositions)).

```lean
[open](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Namespaces-and-Sections/#Lean___Parser___Command___open) Classical
```

```lean
noncomputable def linv [[Inhabited](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#Inhabited___mk) α] (f : α → β) : β → α :=
fun b : β => [if](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Terms/Conditionals/#termDepIfThenElse) ex : (∃ a : α, f a = b) [then](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Terms/Conditionals/#termDepIfThenElse) choose ex [else](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Terms/Conditionals/#termDepIfThenElse) [default](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#Inhabited___mk)
```

```lean
theorem linv_comp_self {f : α → β} [[Inhabited](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#Inhabited___mk) α]
(inj : ∀ {a b}, f a = f b → a = b)
: [linv]](#tpil-linv) f ∘ f = id :=
[funext](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/The-Type-System/Functions/#funext) fun a =>
have ex : ∃ a₁ : α, f a₁ = f a := ⟨a, [rfl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#rfl-next)⟩
have feq : f (choose ex) = f a := choose_spec ex
calc [linv]](#tpil-linv) f (f a)
_ = choose ex := [rfl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/4.33.0/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#rfl-next)
_ = a := inj feq
```

```lean

```

From a classical point of view, `linv` is a function. From a
constructive point of view, it is unacceptable; because there is no
way to implement such a function in general, the construction is not
informative.
